ing: peeled, in chunks; or use yuca
st: Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Soften banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and use them to line a deep ovenproof pot or roasting pan.
Season the pork with [[2 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Layer the pork on the bottom, then the sweet potato, taro and bananas.
Spread the greens over the top.
Pour the coconut milk and [[1 cup]] water evenly over everything.
Fold the leaves over the food and cover tightly with a lid or foil so steam stays in.
Bake for 2 hours 30 minutes until the pork is very tender and has reached at least 145°F (63°C).
Rest for 10 minutes, then serve everything from the pot with the juices.

ing: very fresh firm white fish fillets
such as mahi-mahi or snapper, cut in half-inch cubes
st: Use the freshest fish and keep it very cold until needed.
Place the fish cubes in a glass bowl with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.75 cup]] lime juice.
Toss gently so all the fish is covered, then cover the bowl.
Chill for 30 minutes until the fish turns opaque and firm.
Drain off about half of the lime juice.
Stir in the onion, tomato, chili and cucumber.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] coconut milk and fold gently.
Taste, add salt if needed, top with [[2 tbsp]] cilantro and serve cold.
Stir the sago with [[1 cup]] warm water in a bowl and leave for 15 minutes to hydrate.
Mash the bananas well and mix into the sago to form a sticky dough.
Shape into small balls about the size of a walnut with wet hands.
Bring [[3 cups]] water to a gentle boil in a large pot.
Drop in the balls carefully and cook 15 minutes until they turn translucent and float.
Meanwhile heat the coconut milk, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] sugar in a small pot for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Lift out the dumplings and add them to the coconut milk.
Simmer 5 minutes and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the sweet potato chunks with [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt on a baking tray.
Roast for 35 minutes, turning once, until soft inside and browned at the edges.
Warm [[1 cup]] coconut milk with [[0.25 tsp]] salt and the pepper in a small pot over low heat for 5 minutes.
Place the roasted potatoes in a dish and pour the coconut milk over them.
Return to the oven for 5 minutes so the flavors soak in, then serve warm.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes, turning.
Pour in the coconut milk, [[1 cup]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the sweet potato, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the greens and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Serve hot with rice or extra sweet potato.
Mix the sago starch, coconut and [[0.25 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Slowly add [[0.75 cup]] warm water and stir until a thick dough forms.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes so the starch absorbs the water.
Divide into 6 balls and flatten each into a thin round with your palm.
Heat a dry cast iron skillet or griddle over medium heat and brush with [[1 tbsp]] coconut oil.
Cook each cake for 3 to 4 minutes per side until firm and lightly browned.
Serve warm with fish, greens or a drizzle of coconut milk.
